chunks: about a man who stands in salat (prayer), then looks after he has finished, and sees that he had deviated from the qiblah to the right or the left.
So he said to him: "His salat (prayer) has passed as valid, and what lies between the east and the west is qiblah."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah, the direction faced in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the east, used here as one boundary of accepted direction
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the west, used here as the other boundary of accepted direction
key_terms.شِمَالًا: to the left side, indicating one possible directional deviation
key_terms.قِبْلَةٌ: qiblah, the valid direction of orientation in this context
key_terms.مَضَتْ: has passed, meaning the prayer is considered complete and valid
key_terms.يَمِينًا: to the right side, indicating one possible directional deviation

ai.seo_question: If someone discovers after salat (prayer) that he was slightly off the qiblah, is the prayer still valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who completed salat (prayer) and only afterward realized a slight deviation from the qiblah. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer remains valid, indicating latitude in orientation when the deviation is to the right or left within the general directional span.
